rounds.text: The business is undergoing a clear operational turnaround with profit growth exceeding 1-year price growth by 47%, signaling that it is starting to outperform expectations [E36]. Recent results show robust bottom-line expansion, with compounded profit growth over the trailing twelve months reaching 22% [E16], alongside a remarkable net profit surge of 65% year-over-year [E45], [E48]. This earnings momentum is supported by expanding profitability, as the yearly operating-margin trend has been increasing over the last four years [E23], moving from negative territory to parity in the TTM period [E21] and reaching 1% in the June 2026 quarter [E22]. Furthermore, the company benefits from a supportive macro backdrop, as the chemicals sector is currently in a tailwind with a score of +0.73 [E47], [E49]. Promoters also maintain a committed stake of 62.57% [E32], reflecting stable internal alignment with these improving fundamentals. Conceded: [E12], [E14], [E26], [E30], [E40].

Indian Acrylics Ltd carries severe financial vulnerabilities and structural deterioration that make its current valuation and fundamental health highly questionable. Long-term top-line erosion is glaring, evidenced by compounded sales growth contracting over 10 years (-4%), 5 years (-8%), and 3 years (-27%) [E12, E13, E14], alongside negative long-term share price compression [E17, E18, E19, E20]. The company is deeply leveraged with borrowings escalating to Rs 231 Cr in March 2026 from Rs 183 Cr previously [E30], coupled with a dangerously low interest coverage ratio flag [E38] and a thin current ratio buffer of 1.10x [E29]. Cash generation is alarming, as operating cash flow plunged to a negative Rs -30 Cr and free cash flow dropped to Rs -28 Cr in March 2026 [E26, E27], while promoters have pledged 26.4% of their holding [E40]. Furthermore, reported earnings rely on non-operating crutches like Rs 6.23 Cr in other income [E41], and profitability metrics remain dismal with a negative ROCE of -3.3% [E11] and an inflated EV/EBITDA of 45.4x compared to the sector benchmark of 11.79x [E10]. Conceded: TTM compounded profit growth reached 22% alongside a recent operating margin expansion [E16, E21], and the chemicals sector enjoys a positive tailwind [E47].

Conceded: long-term sales growth has contracted across 10, 5, and 3-year horizons [E12, E13, E14], share price performance has been negative [E17, E18, E19, E20], borrowings increased [E30], interest coverage is flagged as low [E38], cash flows were negative in March 2026 [E26, E27], and promoters have pledged 26.4% of their holdings [E40]. However, dismissing the business ignores a powerful operational turnaround that is actively underway. Compounded profit growth over the trailing twelve months has surged by 22% [E16], with screen metrics capturing a dramatic net profit increase of 65% year-over-year [E45]. Operating margins are expanding, showing a positive year-over-year improvement in the TTM period [E21] and consistent yearly growth over the last four years [E23], supported further by recent quarterly margin gains in June 2026 [E22]. Furthermore, profit growth currently exceeds one-year price growth by 47%, signaling that the company is beginning to outperform stale market expectations [E36]. Conceded: earnings include Rs 6.23 Cr in other income [E41] and ROCE is negative [E11], yet the business operates within a strongly supportive chemical sector tailwind with a score of +0.73 [E47] and trades at an exceptionally high trailing return on equity of 194.69% [E8].

Conceded: profit growth over the trailing twelve months is 22% [E16], screen metrics capture a net profit increase of 65% year-over-year [E45], operating margins show positive year-over-year TTM improvement [E21], and the chemical sector carries a tailwind score of +0.73 [E47]. However, the cited profit surges are heavily inflated by Rs 6.23 Cr in other income rather than core operations [E41], and this temporary accounting benefit masks a severe structural erosion where long-term sales have shrunk by 4% over 10 years, 8% over 5 years, and 27% over 3 years [E12, E13, E14]. The bull emphasizes a high trailing return on equity of 194.69% [E8], but this extreme metric is mathematically distorted by a negative book value of -0.91 [E1] and negative returns on capital employed of -3.3% [E11] and -2.84% [E9]. Furthermore, while margin trends are cited as improving [E21, E23], quarterly margins remain inconsistent over the last two quarters [E24], operating cash flows collapsed to a negative Rs -30 Cr [E26] alongside free cash flow of negative Rs -28 Cr [E27] in March 2026, and borrowings climbed from Rs 183 Cr to Rs 231 Cr [E30] with a flagged low interest coverage ratio [E38] and 26.4% promoter pledge [E40].
